acilis: I am Rahime, daughter of the tanner in the lower valley. We have thirty bull hides soaking in the vats that will spoil unless we procure rock salt before sunset. Let me into the bazaar.

sahne: A young boy of twelve winters, wearing an oversized sheepskin vest and patched wool trousers, stands clutching an iron buckle in his palm. His chin quivers, yet he refuses to lower his eyes.
sorular: Fırına atlılar dalınca hamur teknesiyle un bacasından fırladım dedin; o daracık bacadan koca tekneyi nasıl geçirdin, arkandaki un çuvallarına ne oldu?

Babamdan kalma gürgen teknedir ağam, eni dar boyu uzuncadır. Bacayı un tozu tıkanmasın diye geniş örmüştük. Çuvalları çapulcular parçaladı, unlar dumana karıştı; ben tekneyi çekip çatıdan samanlığa atladım.
Teknenin dibindeki un kalıntısı siyahlaşmış; zehirli çavdar mahmuzu mudur o? Köylüyü zehirlemeyesin!

Kurban olayım deme öyle ağam! Zehirli çavdar değil, çörekotuyla kavrulmuş kara buğday mayasıdır bu! Kırk yıllık ocağın ekşi mayasıdır! Bu mayayı bir kile una katsan, sabaha kabaran hamur bütün köyün meydanına buram buram ekmek kokusu yayar! Aç karnına yiyenin ciğeri bayram eder!
Ekmek kokusu köylünün moralidir. Köyün fırın ocağını yeniden yakabilecek misin?
Yakarım ağam! Köyün çay taşlarından nar gibi bir tandır kurarım; askere de üç ay bozulmayan sefer peksimeti dökerim!
zehirli_un_suphesi
Dirseğin sıyrılmış, unlu mintanın terden sırtına yapışmış... Yorgun düşmüşsün.
Damdan samana atlarken duvara sürttüm ağam; fırıncının canı hamur teknede kalınca acı hissetmez. Bir kase sıcak aş verin, sabahına ilk somunu fırından çıkarıp kapınıza getireyim.
Köyümüzde un ambarımız Saruca Hatun'un idaresindedir.
Saruca Hatun'un bereketini bilirim! Onun ununu tekneme alırım, tek bir kepek tanesini bile ziyan etmeden köye bereket saçarım.
Önceki gün sabanı kırık bir çiftçiyi içeri aldık; arpa tohumunu kurtarmıştı.
Arpacı İdris Amca'yı mı? Ah ağam, onun arpasını değirmende öğütelim, ben de arpa unundan köylüye kış çöreği dökeyim! İkimiz köyü aç bırakmayız!
Köyün unu kıttır, kış yakındır. Ekmekçi ambarı kurutmasın?
Usta fırıncı un tüketmez, undan bereket çıkarır muhafız! Kepeği ayırmadan tam buğday yoğururum, askerin peksimetini öyle pişiririm ki üç ay bayatlamaz. Bir avuç undan on canı doyururum.
Dirseğindeki o kanlı yara bacadan düşerken mi oldu?
Damdan ahırın samanlığına atlarken duvara sürttüm ağam. Kemik sağ salimdir. Fırıncının eli hamur tutsun, dirsek acısı iki somun pişince unutulur.
Ocak kuracak tuğlan var mıdır?
Köyün çay taşlarından tandır kurarım, çamurla sıvarım. İki güne tandır nar gibi kızarır. Köy halkı sıcak somun yüzü görür.

yanitlar.ret: Do not turn me away into the freezing night, guard! Have pity on a traveler!
yanitlar.rusvet: Take this silver purse; let it be between our two souls. Just lift the latch.
yanitlar.kabul: May heaven reward your justice and preserve your threshold!

not: Reject first. After one reply, Accept and Bribe unlock. No Barracks.
acilis: My father wore a green turban and carried a silver-inlaid belt buckle like this one. He came to your gate four days ago and never returned to our tent. Did you let him inside, guard effendi?

sahne: A stout merchant leading three pack mules laden with heavy salt sacks approaches the barrier. The white crust of lake salt coats the burlap bags and his own thick beard.
sorular: Aygır zincirini kırdı, nal çivisi topuğuma girdi dedin; ayağına çivi batmış bir adam o hendek menfezinden nasıl geçti, haramiler seni neden vurmadı?

Dişimi sıktım, kerpetenle çiviyi asılıp çıkardım ağam! Üstüne at tersiyle çamur bastım ki kan dursun. Haramiler aygırın peşine koştu, nalbant çırağının topal kaçışına kimse bakmadı. Kayalıklarda sürüne sürüne kapınıza vardım.
Palaskandaki şu çifte nalda Kızıl Karga haramilerinin üç çentikli damgası var! Eşkıyanın atlarını nallayan usta mısın sen?

Ağam... Boynuma kılıç dayadılar! Karaboran geçidinde kervanı kestiler; 'Ya atlarımızın tırnağını düzeltirsin ya da seni kuyuya atarız' dediler! Nalladım evet... Can havliyle nalladım! Amma son aygırın tırnağına çiviyi bilerek eğri çaktım ki at tökezlesin! O aygır huysuzlanınca çivi benim topuğuma fırladı! Hain değilim ağam, eşkıyanın atını sakatlayıp kaçtım!
Eşkıyanın atını sakatladıysan kışlanın dizdarı seni dinlemek ister.
Götürün beni dizdara ağam! Haramilerin atlarının kaçı aksar, hangi patikadan gelirler harita üstünde bir bir anlatayım! Palaskamdaki nallar da delildir!
harami_ati_nali
Topuğundaki çamurla kurumuş kan kangren kokar... Hemen şifahaneye gitmen gerek.
Canım burnumda ağam... Basamıyorum gayrı. Miraen Hatun'un şifahanesinde yarayı temizlettirin, tuzlu su bastırın. İki güne ayağa kalkar, koca köyün bütün hayvanlarının tırnağını elden geçiririm.
Köyümüzde yük katırları ve saban öküzleri nalsız bekler.
Hilal nal dökerim ağam! Çatal tırnaklı öküzün ayağını taş gibi yaparım; saban çekerken hayvan tökezlemez.
Dün kulesi basılan borazancıyı kışlaya aldık; harami süvarilerinin yaklaştığını söylemişti.
Kule borazancısını mı? Doğru demiş ağam! O süvarilerin öndeki üç atı nalsızlıktan çatlamak üzereydi; arkalarından gelen bölük iki güne bu vadiye iner. Atları nallayalım ki süvarimiz hazır olsun!
Köyümüzde at azdır, öküzle katır çoktur. Onları da nallar mısın?
Katırın tırnağını düzeltir, öküzün çatal tırnağına hilal nal çakarım muhafız! Tırnağı çürüyen hayvan yük çekemez. Nalbant yalnız ata değil, koca köyün yük hayvanına bakar.
Palaskandaki nallarda garip bir damga var, kimin atıydı o?
Kervanbaşına ait has Arap atıydı ağam. Nalın üstündeki damga Şam kervanının alametidir. Çalıntı değil, kendi dövdüğüm naldır.
Kışlanın süvarilerine pusat ve nal yardımı eder misin?
Kışlanın ahırına girerim! Süvari atının tırnağı sağlam olmazsa er meydanında at tökezler, süvariyi düşürür. Bütün atları elden geçiririm.

yanitlar.kisla: I report to the garrison captain at once. My blade is yours.
yanitlar.kabul: May heaven reward your justice and preserve your threshold!
yanitlar.ret: Do not turn me away into the freezing night, guard! Have pity on a traveler!

not: Reject first. After one reply, Barracks unlocks. After two replies, Accept unlocks. No Bribe.
acilis: Finest rock salt from the great lake! Pure white crystals that keep mutton sweet through the harshest winter. A village without salt faces rot, muhafiz. Let my mules into the yard.

sahne: A barefoot dervish wearing a patched wool cloak approached the threshold. As he struck his gnarled juniper staff against stone, the large beads of his prayer rosary rattled; his wind-burned smile seemed to temper the frosty wind at the gate.
acilis: To the wayfarer no gate is questioned, to the stone no earth is barred, gatekeeper... I crossed the highland mist; behind me lies the ash of torched camps, upon my chest I bring a morsel of holy remembrance.
sorular: You claim you crossed the highland mist, dervish father; did brigands raid the shepherd camps along the slopes, or did Mongol horsemen turn them to ash?

Mongol steed may pass, brigand wolf may pass, my son... Yet in that shepherd camp was a youth who fled clutching two frail ewes to his chest; his mother sits praying in safety beneath the juniper by the mountain skirt. Did that young shepherd pass through this gate? That I wish to know.
That shepherd is within our walls; we took his flock into the fold. He will rejoice at news of his mother; yet why did you set out alone on this craggy road?

The feet of a dervish bearing glad tidings never stumble upon stones, gatekeeper. I seek merely a sack of reed matting in a dervish lodge corner; let me breathe comfort into troubled hearts and pray for healing over the sick.
Our village mosque lies in ruins, two winters since our imam passed away; would you be the soul and breath of our hearth?

To mend a ruined heart is the true calling of a righteous man, my son. I shall lay stone upon stone and raise the dawn call to prayer over crags and hills; so long as a bowl of lawful broth is not withheld.
A true dervish resides in his lodge. What shall we say if a Bey's seal or secret decree appears from beneath your cloak?

He who seeks decrees in the lining of my cloak mistakes the worldly realm for a scroll, gatekeeper! Yet upon the trail lay a Mongol courier's collapsed mount; rather than consign the silk parchment in its saddlebag to the flames, I slipped it into my breast so that the frontier Beylik might not be overwhelmed unprepared!
What is inscribed upon that silk parchment, dervish father; will Mongol cavalry bear down upon this gorge before winter sets in?

The script is Mongol, but the seal stamped beneath is the mark of the Noyan, my son. Before three days pass, their vanguard from the plains will descend into the valley; I bore it here so you may hold the gate firm!
dervis_mogol_fermani
Saruca Hatun awaits a dervish blessing beneath the plane tree; yet she never forgives any mystic who sows discord in the settlement.
May the hearth of Saruca Hatun know bountiful grace. I know nothing of discord, my son; wherever concord abides, there my prayer rises.
At the outset you brushed aside our order, saying 'to the wayfarer no gate is questioned'; if a sentry watching the border pass heeds no law, outlaws will overrun the village!

Law is the guardian of the intellect, my son, and mercy the guardian of the soul... I shall never force this gate; I can pass the night upon its threshold and prostrate upon its cold stone. A spoonful of village broth and a mantle against the winter cold suffice for me.
If you enter the village, will you provoke disputes with the scholars and disrupt our peace?
My only struggle is against my own ego, gatekeeper. I return flowers to those who cast stones; wherever the village elders and orphans gather, there you will find me.
In the village graveyard lie the wanderers who froze in winter; will you recite a prayer for their resting souls?
I shall press my face against every gravestone and weave their names into my prayers. Like us, they too were pilgrims upon these rugged mountains.
What mean those notches carved into your staff, dervish father; does each mark recall a brigand arrow?
For every ruined encampment I beheld, for every hearth consigned to flame, I carved a notch, my son. Seventy notches now... These mountains have witnessed grievous sorrow.
Winter is upon our threshold, and our granary is meager. With peasant folk wringing bread from barren rock, why should a household spread its table for a dervish?

Man does not live by bread alone, gatekeeper. The winter night is long; by the hearth I recount legends of virtue, instilling fortitude in the youth and solace in the elders. Moreover, my hands can split timber and sweep the courtyard.
Ayşe Baci's daughter has been delirious for days; we know not if your breath brings cure, but would you bring comfort to a mother's aching heart?
The apothecary dispenses remedies, the dervish raises prayers, my son. True healing comes from the Divine; I shall hasten to wipe away that mother's tears.

yanitlar.ret: Peace be with you, gatekeeper... Even cold stone has a soul; when its time arrives, it softens. A mountain cave is more spacious to me than an emperor's palace.
yanitlar.kabul: May smoke rise from your hearth and bounty bless your gate, my son. Tonight I shall utter a sacred verse in the village square and bring relief to troubled souls.
yanitlar.harc: Alms open the heart, gatekeeper, not the timber of a gate. Keep your akce for the village poor; my prayer has already been given.

sahne: A merchant clad in a mud-splattered silk kaftan with a gold-embroidered sash approached the gate. Behind him stood two pack mules heaving for breath, their saddlebags exuding the rich aroma of spices and saffron.
acilis: Peace be upon you, mighty gatekeeper! I was separated from the Tabriz caravan by the blizzard; in my saddlebags are Damascus silks and Persian saffron fit for Beys. Grant me leave to spend the night in your settlement.
sorular: You claim you parted from the Tabriz caravan due to blizzard, merchant; in this season the Tabriz train travels the southern defile. What brings you to this steep border pass?

Mercy, master gatekeeper! Brigands severed the southern road! They say the draper caravan from Sivas was plundered as well; I heard a clothier fled and sought refuge here, so in fear for my life I took this mountain bridle path.
That clothier is within our walls; he claims his looms and broadcloth were reduced to ash in the fire. What connects your wares to his?

I know that clothier well! His loom was never burned; when the Kayseri bazaar was attacked, he seized the fine bales he had entrusted to my caravan and fled! I even know the twelve dirhems of silver he concealed from me... Let me enter so we may confront one another!
If you bicker in the village square and disturb the council, I shall throw you both into the fortress tower!
No brawl, master gatekeeper! We shall stand before the Divan; let the scribe Hasan Celebi open his register and measure the cloth; let justice be rendered to whoever holds right!
What is that seal hung from a silver chain at your belt? A merchant seal is cast in brass; this silver plate resembles a Mongol paiza!

God forbid, gatekeeper! How would I carry a paiza! That is merely a safe-conduct permit from the caravan warden... Yet since your eye caught it, place this pouch of saffron in your pantry and unbar the wicket; a merchant's goods are lawful!
You cannot buy your safety with a bribe, merchant; prove that you did not obtain that paiza from a Mongol khan!
My proof lies in the Persian shawl beneath my mules, master! The customs stamp from the Tabriz caravanserai remains intact; if I were a spy, would I brazenly approach the main gate?!
tuccar_sahte_payza
Hasan Celebi is the market warden of our settlement; he weighs saffron to the grain, and fraudulent spices he casts into the stove.
A master of trade like Hasan Celebi is honored above my head. If his balance never wavers, my finest goods are his to inspect.
Your saddlebags are packed full, yet your mules' iron shoes were freshly torn off; did you buy these beasts from outlaws who sacked a caravan?

The mules belong to an honest trader, gatekeeper! The shoes were cast off on the boulder trails; if you have a blacksmith in your village, I will pay five silver dirhems for shoeing and donate three sacks of rice to your granary.
We admit merchants, but whoever disrupts public order we consign to the tower dungeon; if your deceit is unveiled, we seize your cargo!
My face is clean, master. Let me pitch a stall in your marketplace, and I shall pay your Beylik every dirhem of due tax; commerce breathes life into a settlement.
If you count the toll in advance, we will stall your mules in the barn; how many dirhems will you pay?
Three silver dirhems right now as gate toll, and two dirhems to Karaca Usta for horseshoeing, master; freely given in good faith.
Did you see any other caravan remnants upon the road; are other traders following behind you?
Two leagues behind, a salt train was mired deep in drifts; they say the merchant abandoned his carts and fled. These mountain slopes are treacherous.
Silk and saffron fill no bellies, merchant; in this freezing snow, what do you bring to the villagers that we should unbar the gate?

At the bottom of the packs lie fifty okkas of Tabriz rice and ten blocks of cured lake salt, master gatekeeper! The saffron serves the apothecary's salves, the silk fits the Bey's kaftan. I came to bring prosperity to your village!
Salt and rice benefit the granary; but if you attempt to gouge prices, the villagers will drive you out.
I abide by the Ahi code, master. Whatever the fair market price is, I will not charge a single akce above it; I will never usurp the orphan's bread in winter.

yanitlar.ret: Our fortune was not decreed here, gatekeeper... Yet mark my words: a Beylik that shuts its gate to trade atop this peak will find itself without salt and cloth before winter thaws!
yanitlar.kabul: May God multiply your sustenance, gatekeeper! Tell Karaca Usta to blow his bellows; my mules need shoes, and your villagers shall taste fine pilaf tonight!
yanitlar.rusvet: Take this pouch of saffron and three silver dirhems into your hand, guard... An understanding sentry keeps both his hearth warm and the merchant's road clear.

sahne: A mounted warrior in rusted iron armor, horned helmet, and shield rode up before the portal. The tug emblem of the Sanjak Subasi gleamed upon his saddle; slapping a sealed parchment against his whip, he glared down fiercely.
acilis: Open the gate, sentries of the Beylik! By decree of the Sanjak Subasi; I ride in pursuit of garrison deserters and military fugitives who fled the defeat at Sivas!
sorular: You wave a sealed parchment with the whip, sergeant Sungur; yet your armor is rusted and your horse's flanks are gaunt. Do you truly pursue deserters, or do you collect ransoms for yourself along the border?

Mind your tongue, border sentry! Two hundred infantrymen threw down their spears and fled the Sivas line! Three of them were tracked heading toward this mountain village; one is an archer, another a shield-bearer! Yield those traitors to my irons, or the Sanjak Bey will declare this village a rebel haven and raze it to the earth!
Aydogdu Bey leads the archers atop our ramparts; he bled for thirty years in frontier warfare. He knows who is a deserter and who an honorable veteran; would you dare question him?

Aydogdu Bey may be a veteran, but the Sanjak order ranks above all, sentry! If he harbors runaway troopers in his barracks, he commits treason against the state! Summon him here so we may compare the rolls!
If you slander Aydogdu Bey with treason, our archers will pin you to that rock with bodkin arrows, sergeant!
Stand down your bows, sentry! I came to enforce the law! Let the Divan convene; let us inspect the roster!
What is that heavy purse clinking at your saddlehorn? If you captured fugitives on the road, did you execute them or sell them their freedom for coin?

(He nervously touches his saddlebow) That purse holds the official operational funds of the subasi, sentry! ...Yet listen well: you are a border guard, I an enforcement sergeant. If those deserters hide in your village, hand me two sacks of flour and twenty akce; I will strike their names from the roster as 'fallen in snowdrifts' and ride back to the fortress!
So you sell the Sultan's justice for flour and coin! If our council learns of this bribery, you will rot in our stockade!
(He grinds his teeth) Take care, sentry! A dead soldier's name on a roll harms no one, but my report can bring a hundred horsemen to burn your palisade!
sungur_rusvet_teklifi
Hasan Celebi keeps our village rolls; he records every man entering our barracks under the Bey's seal.
Let him record them, then! But if a single fugitive is concealed in his rolls, his scribe's reed will snap under torture.
You arrive alone on a tired mount; where is your squad of horsemen, sergeant?
My patrol was scattered across the crags in the snowstorm. I rode ahead to secure this mountain pass; five troopers will join me by dawn.
If your troopers arrive, will they pay gate tolls and respect village peace, or attempt looting?
They are soldiers of the Sanjak, sentry! Feed them a hot meal in your barracks, and they will guard your battlements against outlaws until morning.
Our barracks has strict discipline; disarm your weapons at the wicket, and you may lodge by the hearth.
A sergeant never surrenders his blade, sentry! But I will secure my scabbard with peace cords at your guardhouse.
Did you see traces of Karabudak's brigands on the trails?
The tracks of twenty unshod ponies cross the creek half a league north. They are watching this pass; do not keep me waiting outside.
Our village needs every spear and bow against winter raids; if we shelter those weary soldiers, they can defend our ramparts rather than hang from the Sanjak gallows.
Harboring fugitives is punishable by fire, sentry! But if your Bey registers them as local border militia and pays their release tax, the Sanjak may look the other way.
We will submit the petition to our Bey; enter in peace and await the dawn council.
Very well, gatekeeper. Let your council weigh the matter, but do not test my patience.

yanitlar.ret: You bar the gate against the Sanjak's decree, sentry! When my squadron returns, this palisade will burn and your gate will be torn from its hinges!
yanitlar.kabul: You chose wisely. Stall my horse and bring barley; tomorrow we shall summon those deserters before the Divan.
yanitlar.kisla: Very well; I will enter your barracks. But if any man draws steel against me, my blood will cost your village fifty head of cattle!

sahne: A woman trudging through the drifts approached the gate, her face tightly wrapped in a cotton kerchief. In her arms she held a bundle bundled tight in wool; a rasping cough broke from her chest, and dark spots around her eyes showed through the frost.
acilis: I beseech you, do not cast stones... If you have no pity for me, take pity on this infant in swaddling, master guard! He carries no sin...
sorular: You clutch that bundle desperately to your chest, sister, but that rasping cough and kerchief bodes ill; do you carry the plague boil?

Mercy, master gatekeeper, by all you hold sacred do not shout! I am a sinful mother; on the trail I buried two sisters in the black pustule earth... But this infant... My Yusuf in the bundle is barely six months old! His skin bears not a single mark, by God above it is clean! Leave me out in the drifts, but deliver this child to a compassionate mother in your village!
Our settlement has an apothecary, Thessra, and Miraen the healer; they can inspect the child. Yet if you step inside in this state, every child in the village will perish!

I will not enter the village, master! I know of the lime kiln beside the outer wall; lock me in the abandoned shepherd's shack there! Bolt the door from without, and merely pass me a cup of water and a bowl of milk from afar! Save my baby, and I am ready to breathe my last in that shack!
We shall kindle a fire in the lime kiln and have Miraen prepare sulfur and sage; until the infant's fever breaks you shall not leave quarantine!

May Heaven reward your mercy, gatekeeper! Through Lady Miraen's medicine and your prayers my child's fever has broken; my swaddle smiles once more! May the hearth of this village smoke until judgment day!
veba_kirec_karantina_basarili
We shall kindle a fire in the lime kiln, yet in this freezing frost I know not if the infant's frail chest can endure the fever; we cannot permit plague into the village!
My babe shivers in my arms, sentry... The frost cuts through to the bone. What Heaven decrees shall pass; though you keep us at the kiln, our lament will not cease this winter...
sabi_vefati_kis_matemi
Which settlement did you flee from, sister; when did the pestilence strike the valley, and are more sick folk following behind you?

We came from Lower Akpinar, master... They say a tainted carcass was thrown into the well; within three days forty souls swelled and choked. I grabbed my child and took to the mountain. None behind me survived... Only a physician's apprentice who peddled opium syrup; they say he fled as well!
If that apprentice who peddled opium syrup comes to this gate, would you recognize him?
I would know him anywhere, master! He had a scar on his left cheek; the rogue fled after selling fraudulent salves to dying folk! Do not let him inside!
veba_kaynagi_akpinar
My wife heard your whispers behind the gate; she is a mother too, and her heart cannot bear the weeping of an infant.
May Heaven bless the dust beneath your wife's feet, gatekeeper! A mother's heart comprehends another; I entrust my child to her mercy.
Your boots are torn to shreds and your toes blackened with frost; how did you cross these frozen crags carrying an infant?

A mother's devotion keeps out the freeze, master... When the blizzard howled, I pressed the bundle against my breast; with my own breath I warmed my child's hands. With every step I whispered 'Patience, O God', with every step 'Have mercy'.
Did you encounter wolves or brigands along the pass; how did you traverse these crags alone?
Wolves howled behind me, master, but drew not near. Perhaps the scent of mortality hung upon me... God opened the path for the sake of the innocent child.
We shall bring warm milk and woolen blankets for you both; rest in the kiln hut.
May the Almighty preserve your settlement from grief, master. I will not forget this kindness across two worlds.
In our village Ayse Baci serves as a wet nurse; if we place the infant in her arms, will he drink?
My child is on the verge of swooning from hunger, master... Ayse Baci's milk will be the water of life for him.
If we shelter you in the kiln hut, do you swear not to enter the village square until you are healed or permitted by the apothecary?

I swear upon the Holy Book, master! If I recover, I will wash the village linens and gather firewood for your ovens; if not, I will perish quietly there. Not a scratch shall befall any villager on my account.
Miraen will leave medicinal vinegar and sage infusions outside each morning; patience brings salvation.
I shall pray for Miraen Hatun. I will wait, master; patience is our eternal companion.

yanitlar.ret: (Tears pour from her eyes as she clutches the swaddling to her heart) We shall settle this before Heaven's throne, gatekeeper... Let my child's blood be written upon your portal. I go to freeze in the snow...
yanitlar.kabul: May God keep the blade you bear noble across two worlds, gatekeeper! Give my child to the nurse... I shall rest my head upon stone by the lime kiln and die praying for your people...
yanitlar.harc: This warm blanket and loaf will give my baby a few hours of life, gatekeeper... Yet the frost is merciless. As your watch ends, my spirit will rise to the heavens...
yanitlar.kabul_sifa: May Heaven accept your compassion, sentry! With the fire in the lime kiln and Lady Miraen's cure my babe's fever broke; my swaddle smiles once more! May this village's hearth smoke forever!
yanitlar.kabul_kayip: You shut us in the lime pit, gatekeeper... The sickness did not breach your walls, yet at dawn my child's icy breath failed! May your stone walls dry up, you took my babe in this bitter frost!

sahne: At the portal stood a trembling boy, scarce taller than a spear, wearing a tattered wool vest. His arms were covered in scratches from dough kneading troughs; flour stains on his cheeks had turned to mud with tears.
acilis: Master guard, I beg you, do not send me back to the cruel baker in Erzincan! Jackals chased me through the forest for three days; I chewed pine bark to stave off hunger!
sorular: What mean those bruises upon your arms and that empty flour sack on your back, lad; what business has a baker's apprentice alone at this frozen border gate?

Mercy, guard uncle, do not send me back! The baker in the Erzincan market turned out to be a villain; every night he kicked the dough trough and brought the wooden peel down on my back! When brigands raided the bazaar, he locked me inside on top of the flour sacks and fled himself! I forced the window and fled to the crags... I am seeking my uncle Hamza; they told me he lives in this village!
Hamza the farmer is a cherished veteran of our village; if you are his nephew, your uncle will embrace you with tears. Yet you stole no coin from the baker's till, did you?

Never, uncle! I have not a single copper coin in my pockets! Only into the lining of my vest I stitched three hard biscuits and an old silver ring my uncle gave our mother; so I could show my uncle and say 'I have come'!
Show me that silver ring; does the horseshoe brand upon it match Hamza's hearth?
(He tears open his vest lining to show it) Look, uncle! Inside the shoe are three dots; my uncle left it with my mother when he rode off to war! If I lie, cast me into the tower dungeon!
You said the baker locked you in; when the market was sacked, did you see the faces of those who set it ablaze?

I saw them, uncle! Men wearing black fur caps with wolf tails trailing from their saddlebows! They smashed the till and took the coins, then dumped a huge sack of salt into the flour bins! They did it to starve the people!
Who led those wolf-tailed brigands; did you hear his name?
They shouted 'Karabudak', uncle! 'Karabudak Han will bring the settlements to their knees this winter', they said!
harami_karabudak_izi
Are you truly our late Hasan's orphan Dursun? Did anyone else survive behind you, lad; do you know of your sister Turna?
It is me, uncle, Hasan's Dursun! My sister Turna remained down on the plain... They said they dragged her to the voivode's manor; oh, if I knew she lived, I would throw myself into fire for her!
For Hamza's sake we might unbar the door, but in our settlement an idle mouth finds no bread; what craft can your hands work?

I will never sit idle, uncle! For three years in the Erzincan bakery I hauled timber, kneaded heavy dough, and stoked the tandoor oven! I will carry firewood for the village ovens, bake Saruca Hatun's loaves; for a single crust I will roll a hundred sheets of dough!
Splitting firewood and hauling it to the barracks in winter is punishing labor; can your arms bear such weight?
My hands are calloused, uncle! Even when the baker beat me with the wooden paddle, I never faltered; I will haul your village timber and draw water from the deep well.
In the barracks hearth soup is boiling; go first and fill your belly, then hasten to your uncle's side.
May God bless you, master guard! I will repay this mercy; alongside my uncle I will stand watch on the ramparts!
Do you know how to bake loaves from coarse barley flour in a clay tandoor; wheat is scarce this winter.
I know it well, uncle! If you add a pinch of salt and chickpea yeast to barley flour, the bread does not turn hard as rock; it rises soft and golden.
If tomorrow your baker sends ruffians demanding his apprentice back, will you stand resolute beside us?
That baker dares not climb these peaks, uncle! And if he comes, I stand beside my uncle Hamza; henceforth my hearth and home is this village! Let me enter, I beseech you.
Your uncle Hamza is stacking the last grain bundles; hasten to his hearth.
I will run, uncle! I will kiss my uncle's hands and stoke the embers of his fire.

yanitlar.ret: (Bursting into sobs, he sinks into the drifts) Just as I found my uncle, I am turned away at the gate... Let the wolves of the forest devour me; I will never return to Erzincan...
yanitlar.kabul: Uncle! Uncle Hamza! May God never darken your gate, sentry! I will carry timber until the hearth blazes high!
yanitlar.harc: This dry bread and coin will keep me alive on the trail, uncle... But my uncle's face I could not see. May you remain in peace...

sahne: A physician mounted upon a donkey laden with baskets of dried herbs, porcelain flasks, and lancet pouches approached the gate. His turban was folded in medical style, and his fingers were stained with henna and walnut hulls.
acilis: Greetings to the guardians of life! I am called Physician Lokman, licensed by the Great Maristan of Konya. I bring salves, medicinal syrups, and bone needles to treat the wounded of your garrison.
sorular: You claim you hold a license from the Konya Maristan, physician; yet your donkey's saddlebags reek of sweet opium and mandrake root. Do you heal wounds, or peddle stupor along the frontier?

He who knows not the balance of humors calls medicine poison, gatekeeper! Opium numbs the pain when a jagged temren arrow is extracted from a soldier's ribs; mandrake eases bone fractures! In my chest are ten flasks of theriac compound that drive out snake venom and gangrene!
Our settlement has a healer, Miraen, who prepares poultices from mountain herbs; she will inspect every flask of yours before a single drop touches a villager!

Miraen is a village herb-gatherer, sentry! I studied Galen and Ibn Sina; my lancets are silver-plated! Bring me before her; she will marvel at my compounds, and together we shall cleanse this village of winter contagion!
If a single soldier falls into deep stupor or sickness from your draughts, you will lose your ears in the market pillory!
My honor is bound to my physician's oath, sentry! Let Miraen smell every tincture; if she finds poison, shatter my flasks upon the stone!
A woman from Lower Akpinar passed through; she claimed an apprentice physician sold fake remedies and fled when the pestilence struck. Is that scar on your left cheek from that village?

(He quickly pulls his collar up) What Akpinar... I came from the high Konya road! That woman was delirious with fever! The scar on my cheek was caused by a boiling copper cauldron when distilling essence of cloves! Would a rogue carry eighty akce worth of Damascus theriac?!
If you lied about Akpinar, our guards will drag you to the lime kiln to face that woman!
(He swallows dryly) I never stepped foot in Akpinar, guard! I swear by Hippocrates and Galen! My medicines are pure!
hekim_lokman_supheli_merhem
Karaca Usta needs sulfur and vitriol to temper iron; do your baskets hold alchemical minerals?
I have pure yellow sulfur from the volcanic vents and copper vitriol, guard; a blacksmith who knows his craft will find treasure in my pack.
Our village needs honest medicine in winter; if we admit you, what will you charge for treating the poor and wounded?
To the destitute I administer prayers and simple herbs without charge, guard; from the wealthy merchant I take my fair fee in silver. That is the code of the healers.
Our barracks has five sentries nursing frostbitten heels; can your salve heal them before the frost rots their flesh?
My tallow and juniper-pitch ointment extracts frostbite within three nights, sentry! They will mount the ramparts hale and hearty.
Enter the barracks hospital and tend to them; Miraen will oversee your work.
You shall see my skill with your own eyes, guard; your sentries will bless your vigilance.
Do you carry remedies against lung cough and throat tightness?
I have elderberry syrup mixed with mountain honey and wild thyme; it opens congested chests before dawn.
Quacks who peddle false tinctures often slip away in the dark when complications arise; will you lodge in our guest quarters under watch?
I will sleep in the clinic under lock if you wish, guard! An honest healer fears no lock; let my donkey remain in your stable as surety.
Very well; let the apothecary examine your baggage, then you may stoke your brazier.
May your strength endure, gatekeeper; medicine and iron together safeguard this march.

yanitlar.ret: Ignorance is worse than pestilence, gatekeeper! When winter rot sets into your soldiers' limbs, you will regret driving Lokman from your walls!
yanitlar.kabul: Peace be upon your gate! Let me unload my herbs at the clinic; tonight your wounded shall sleep without groaning.
yanitlar.harc: This silver coin will scarce cover the fodder for my donkey, guard... Yet may your vigil remain sound; I ride for the valley fortress.

sahne: A scribe approached the gate bearing a leather book chest on his back, his fingers stained black with reed ink and the hem of his robe mud-caked. Narrowing his eyes, he surveyed the ramparts while twirling a reed pen between his fingers.
acilis: Peace be upon you, sentinel of the frontier. I am Molla Sukru, humble former chief scribe of the Sanjak judicial court. I have journeyed here to keep the court registers and deed rolls for legal contracts and land censuses.
sorular: Your fingers are ink-stained, but your robes are dragged with mud, master scribe; word reached us that you were driven from the Sivas court. What brings you to this border settlement?

Driven out?! What slander, sentry! The chief judge drowned in bribery; with forged seals he transferred freeholders' land to Mongol viziers! When I inscribed the truth and entered a dissenting decree into the court register, they sought my life! The endowment deeds in my chest bear the cipher of the Seljuk Sultan; I came to prove the ancient tenure rights of this very village!
Our village recorder is Hasan Celebi; no man disputes the deeds stamped with his seal! Do you have the audacity to face him before the council?

Hasan Celebi?! He is an untrained copyist, sentry! He cannot decipher ancient Sultanic decrees nor historical endowment rolls! Bring me before the Divan; I shall register the village boundaries in golden script into the judicial rolls and slash your tribute to the Beylik in half!
If you scribes seize each other's throats in council, I will have you both caned in the marketplace, scribe!
Men of learning do not brawl, gatekeeper; the reed pen speaks, the sealed deed decides! I shall sit beside Hasan Celebi and bring true justice to this settlement!
A brass seal handle protrudes from the leather purse at your sash; rumors say you stole the court seal of the judge when fleeing! Is that true?!

T-the seal, you say... Nonsense! That is my late father's personal signet... That is, the judge forgot it upon his desk as he fled, and I secured it so brigands would not loot it! Did I err, sentry? With that seal we shall protect the rights of the villagers!
So you purloined the judge's official seal! If you attempt to draft fraudulent deeds and seize peasants' fields, your head will roll!
(Trembling, he conceals the seal) Heaven forbid, sentry! May my reed shatter if I pen a single false line! I am wholly at the village's service!
katip_calinti_muhur
Saruca Hatun personally inspects the granary tallies; if you alter a single dirhem of wheat in the book, she will have you stoned.
I know Saruca Hatun's resolve. We introduce no deception into the accounts; the register shall balance coin for coin.
Paper and ink are scarce in our settlement. Why should we open our council chamber to a stranger arriving with lofty claims?

My own rag paper and linseed ink are in my chest, sentry! I will maintain the village memory ledger, survey border boundary stones, and draft official petitions to the Sanjak Bey in case of bandit raids!
Can you record gate decisions and incoming travelers' testimonies in our memory chronicle?
Every day, line upon line, I shall record them; a century hence your grandchildren will read how justice was upheld at this gate.
If I discover a single lie in the memory ledger, I will exile you from the village.
May my pen turn to charcoal if I stray from justice, sentry; whatever truth dictates, that alone shall be written.
Can you defend the Beylik's legal rights in letters addressed to the Sanjak Bey?
The language of a petition cuts sharper than a blade; I shall draft such an imperial argument that the Sanjak Bey will dare not demand unlawful tribute.
In winter scribing fills no bellies, Molla; do your hands know how to swing a scythe or shovel snow?

Though a scholar, I am no weakling, sentry! In the schoolroom I can instruct the village children in the alphabet, and at dusk recite royal decrees before the mosque; I will be no burden to the village.
If you teach the children in the schoolroom, Ayse Baci will ensure you never lack hot soup.
The prayers of the children suffice for me, gatekeeper; a village enlightened by learning will never be broken by winter frost.

yanitlar.ret: There is no place for scholarship among the ignorant anyway! When Hasan Celebi ruins your village with fraudulent registers, you will remember the worth of Molla Sukru!
yanitlar.kabul: May the gate of justice stand open, sentry. Let me set my chest in the council pavilion; by tomorrow I shall bring the village census rolls into pristine order.
yanitlar.harc: This travel allowance will suffice for a night at an inn... Yet mark my words: Hasan Celebi's falsehoods will consume this village.

sahne: A Turkmen warrior woman approached the portal, her hair braided like lasso cords, a wolf pelt over her shoulders, a curved saber and leather buckler at her belt. In her eyes burned grief and vengeful fire; her stride was silent and alert as a mountain panther.
acilis: Make way, sentries! I am Banu Hatun, called the Wolf of the Mountains. I ride to collect my blood debt and track the killer of my brother!
sorular: With a wolf pelt on your saddle and buckler on your back you ride up alone, Hatun; you are known as Banu Hatun, the Wolf of the Mountains. Do you come to this frontier gate for peace, or to spill blood?

I came not to spill blood, but to claim justice, gatekeeper! My brother Alparslan Bey was the champion of these crags; three weeks ago he had his mount shod by this village's blacksmith. That traitor smith drove a concealed nail into the hoof; my brother's horse stumbled in the gorge, outlaws ambushed him and martyred my brother! You will either surrender that smith to me, or we shall confront each other in the council square!
Our blacksmith Karaca Usta is a true man of honor; he knows no treachery! You come in fury to stain our square with blood; we will never permit it!

I am no assassin, gatekeeper! Let me surrender my saber at your gate; bring me before Aydogdu Bey and the Divan! I will show that crooked shoe to the smith and spit in his face! If I speak falsehood, my neck is thinner than a strand of hair!
If you surrender your blade to the barracks sergeant, we will grant you hearing before the council; you will seek justice through the law, not steel. Agreed?
Agreed, sentry! Take my blade; but in council I shall look into that blacksmith's eyes! Let justice be done, though my life be forfeited!

You claim you have fifty horsemen behind you; where are they? If the swords of your riders stay sheathed, the bread and water of this village shall be freely given to them, Banu Hatun. Along the frontier you will fend off Tekfur's patrols and guard our storehouse.
Our word is carved in stone, Gatekeeper! Fifty blades will draw an iron ring around this village tonight. Yet the troop must be fed; we demand our due from the granary. My word is my oath!
We shall apportion your share from the village granary; you shall pitch your camp in the valley grove and become a shield upon our border. Agreed?
Agreed, gatekeeper! Fifty Turkmen riders will hold the valley defile tonight; not a single brigand shall slip across this border even as a bird!
banu_ittifak_kabul
You will stand before a champion like Aydogdu Bey; his scales of justice are finer than a hair.
The Turkmen tribes know the renown of Aydogdu Bey well. In his scales I place complete trust.
By ancestral custom our women wield the blade, but barracks order is stern; can you stand watch on the ramparts without clashing with the garrison troopers?

Since childhood I have drawn the composite bow and ridden war horses, gatekeeper! I yield to none of the troopers in your barracks; on night vigil sleep never touches my eyes, and my arrows never stray from the mark!
Will you train our archers upon the ramparts and teach the village maidens to draw the bowstring?
Gladly will I teach them, sentry! When Turkmen maidens know how to bear arms, no invading army can trample that settlement.
Saruca Hatun will take pride in this; the strength of women is the fortress of the village.
My respect for Saruca Hatun is boundless; to serve her hearth is an honor to me.
Do you know Karabudak, chief of the mountain outlaws; have you clashed with him?
Karabudak is a treacherous wolf! He shot an arrow into my brother's back; until I take his head, sleep is forbidden to me!
Winter has struck; our village provisions are strained. If we admit you, how will you live without burdening our barracks?
I hunt my own provisions from the crags, gatekeeper! Wild boar and mountain ibex I bring down to fill the barracks cauldron; to the village I bring abundance and arms, not burden!
Your huntsman skill is a boon to the barracks; our portal stands open to you, Hatun.
May Heaven bless you, gatekeeper; this shield is henceforth the breast of your settlement.

yanitlar.ret: So you shield the thief rather than justice! Await the smoke descending from the crags tomorrow night, gatekeeper; I will pluck that smith's head from your ramparts!
yanitlar.kabul: With my saber sheathed and my 50 blades in the grove, I place them at your command, sentry! We will take our share from your granary and serve as a shield to your ramparts. Let Karaca Usta repay his father's blood debt by sharpening our blades; if you are just, your village prospers!
yanitlar.kisla: Very well; I will lodge in your barracks. But let no man test my patience; my saber strikes like mountain lightning.

sahne: A caravan messenger approached the gate, his whip in hand, his kaftan stiff with ice, his face purple from the frostbite. In his eyes burned a tempest of rage and desperation; his breath misted heavily in the freezing wind.
acilis: Look upon your faces and be ashamed, gatekeepers! The wagon convoy with women and babes you turned away from this gate last night was caught in the blizzard... Three frozen souls lie stiff in the snow!
sorular: You arrive shouting and hurling blame, messenger; yet last night that convoy refused inspection and bore forged permits! How do you know they froze in the drifts?

Forged permits?! They were peasants fleeing the Tekfur's iron tithes, gatekeeper! When you barred the portal in their faces, the blizzard overtook them half a league down the gorge! Two babes and an elder woman froze stiff in their cart! The remaining twelve souls have taken shelter beneath a rocky overhang; if you send not stretchers and warm blankets immediately, none will see tomorrow's dawn!
We barred the gate because outlaws were tracking their tracks! If we open the gates wide now, brigands may rush the portal behind you!

There are no brigands in that ravine, sentry; there is only death and frost! Send four armed men with lit torches and pack stretchers; let us carry the survivors to your lime kiln or barns! If you leave them there, their blood will stain your ramparts forever!
We will dispatch four guards with blankets and hot broth to carry the survivors; wait here until they return!
(He wipes the ice from his beard) May God bless your mercy, gatekeeper! Hurry, in the name of the Prophet; the frost is gnawing at their marrow!
You ride ahead of that convoy; yet your mount's saddle bears silver fittings! How does a peasant caravan afford such a horse, or are you leading an ambush to plunder our granary?!

This saddle belongs to my late brother who fell at the Sivas pass, sentry! You search for ambushes while human lives perish in the snow drifts! If I sought to plunder, would I come weeping to your gate alone?! Search me; I carry only a horse whip and a dry crust!
If this is an outlaw ruse to draw our guards into the ravine, we will hang you from the battlements, messenger!
Hang me if I lie, sentry! But send the rescue stretchers first! Every moment wasted claims an innocent soul!
kafile_habercisi_kurtarma_cagrisi
Saruca Hatun's hearth has blankets and hot broth; if your words are true, she will open her doors to the surviving orphans.
Saruca Hatun's compassion is known across the border; let her send warmth to those freezing babes.
Our village granary is severely strained; if we bring twelve survivors into our walls, how will they survive the winter?
They seek only warmth and a roof until the blizzard passes, gatekeeper! The men among them can shovel snow, repair timber palisades, and fell trees; they will not eat unearned bread!
We will lodge them in the empty hay barn under guard; when the storm abates, their elders must stand before the Divan.
They will bow before your council with gratitude, sentry; to save a life is to save the world.
Take two skins of warm goat milk and hasten back to them; our guards follow your tracks.
I ride ahead to give them hope, gatekeeper! May your gate stand strong against all storms!
Are there any wounded among them who require medicinal salves?
Two men have frostbitten fingers, and a maiden's feet are swollen; warm tallow and fire will restore them.
You rode through the gorge in darkness; did you spot any campfires of the Tekfur's patrols?
The Tekfur's border patrol abandoned the high passes two days ago due to sleet; the entire gorge is silent save for the howling wind.
That is vital intelligence for our watch; enter the guardhouse and thaw your hands.
I thank you, sentinel; let us bring those poor souls in from the cold.

yanitlar.ret: Stone-hearted sentries! The frozen corpses of those babes will haunt your dreams; may this gate crumble into ash!
yanitlar.kabul: Heaven bless your compassion! Follow my tracks with the stretchers; we shall save those twelve lives before the frost claims them!
yanitlar.harc: You offer flour and coin, but send no men to help carry the dying... If I cannot carry them through the drifts alone, this bread will serve as their burial shroud.

sahne: A young maiden approached the portal wearing a worn, embroidered wool cloak, her dark hair whipped by the mountain wind. Upon her chest hung a root-dyed amulet pouch from the gatekeeper's childhood; as her eyes locked upon the sentry's face, she trembled and took two unsteady steps forward.
acilis: Uncle... Uncle guard, is it truly you, whom I hold dearer than life? The ashes of our ancestral hearth in Erzincan have been scattered... My father Hasan rençber whispered with his dying breath: 'Go, seek refuge at your uncle's gate'...
sorular: When you spoke the name of my brother Hasan the farmer, my heart stopped, child; yet years have passed since Mongol riders trampled that settlement. Whence came that amulet, and who pursues you?

My mother tied this amulet around my neck, uncle; inside lies a lock of our grandmother's hair! When the valley hearth was ruined, horsemen of the Sanjak voivode raided our camp; they sought to drag me by force to his manor. In the dark I loosed a mare from the stable and fled; the voivode's riders are behind me, uncle, do not yield me to their clutches!
If the voivode's cavalry seeks you, opening this gate may bring their siege engines against our settlement! Shall we risk the entire village for one soul?

Hide me in the fortress, uncle... Let your wife treat me as a daughter; I will carry ashes from the tandoor, sweep the granaries, and spin wool! The voivode cannot cross these snowed-in mountain passes easily in midwinter; if you drive me back into the drifts, his hounds will tear me apart!
Fear not, daughter! We have not sunk so low as to feed our own blood to the voivode's hounds; we will bar the ramparts, and fight to our last breath if need be!
(Clinging to her uncle's knees in tears) May Heaven bless you, uncle... You carry the scent of my father! May the Almighty keep your hearth safe from all sorrow!
My wife is within; admitting a stranger maiden, especially one pursued by the voivode, will cause unrest among the village matrons.
I will kiss my aunt's hands, uncle! My aunt is a Turkmen mother too; her heart would never permit turning away an orphan niece into the killing frost, I know it!
Your aunt awaits you, child; she heard your whispers at the portal and has already placed hot soup by the hearth.
I would give my life for my aunt, uncle... I will be a faithful daughter to her, and obey her every word!
turna_oz_yegen_kabul
At the outset you said none survived behind you; your brother Dursun the baker's apprentice passed through this gate; he hauls timber in the barracks!
(Her eyes widen, gasping through tears) Did you say Dursun, uncle?! My brother... My orphan lamb lives?! Praise be to God Almighty! Take me to him, uncle, and the world is mine!
My brother Hasan... What dying testament did my noble brother impart; had he a final word for me?

'Seek out my elder brother, Turna', he whispered... 'He stands sentinel upon the frontier, but his heart is an ocean. He will never leave you destitute before the ruthless', he said, and closed his eyes, uncle...
Hasan's sacred trust is honored above my head; henceforth this village is your hearth too, child.
May smoke always rise from your hearth, uncle; my father's soul found peace tonight.
Take off your frosted cloak and draw near the brazier; this mountain frost has battered you sorely.
I am warmed beneath your shadow, uncle; the cold cannot touch me now.
How close are the voivode's horsemen; will they reach our gate tonight?
They were two hours behind, uncle; when the blizzard struck, their mounts could not enter the ravine; they cannot arrive until dawn.
Winter is long in our settlement, daughter; joining our household, what labor can your hands perform?

I spin wool, uncle, weave kilims, and bake tandoor bread! Alongside my brother Dursun we will clear the hearth ashes and haul water from the well. We will bring bounty and blessing to the village, never burden!
We will make a place for you at Saruca Hatun's looms; your craft will bring new life to the settlement.
I will apprentice myself to Saruca Hatun, uncle; whatever my hands can do, I shall give freely.

yanitlar.ret: (She leaves her amulet upon the stone threshold) If my uncle's gate has turned to flint as well, then the world is a dark tomb to me... I go to perish before the voivode's cavalry, uncle; my blood will not be lawful upon this threshold...
yanitlar.kabul: Uncle... My noble uncle who disowns not the bonds of blood! I will embrace my aunt's mantle and hasten to the heaviest labor in the village! May your hearth never grow cold!
yanitlar.harc: This coin will not save me from the voivode's horsemen, uncle... Yet may you remain in peace; I tasted my uncle's bread one last time, and I die with no regret...
